title: Investigate & mitigate probe-induced autoscaling regression (HPA + KEDA noise)
creator: Aisha Patel
description: After a capacity event on 2026-03-09 we observed repeated scale-ups and scale-downs in the realtime-inference pool. The symptoms looked like HPA and KEDA oscillation with frequent 1->3->1 replica flips, increased cold-start latency, and transient 429s for critical customer routes. This ticket captures timeline, root cause analysis, and a prioritized mitigation plan.
timeline: 2026-03-09 02:17 UTC - First alert: realtime-inference request error rate > 2% and p95 latency increased from 120ms to 1.4s.
2026-03-09 02:19 UTC - KEDA scaler triggered scale from 1 -> 3 replicas based on custom metric (queue_depth) spike; HPA did not register immediate CPU pressure.
2026-03-09 02:23 UTC - After new pods started, readiness probe failures surged (probe timeouts ~3s) causing some pods to briefly fail readiness and rejoin, emitting short-lived metric gaps.

2026-03-09 02:30 UTC - KEDA observed repeated short spikes in queue_depth (seconds-long) and initiated multiple additional scale events; autoscaler cooldowns did not prevent repeated scaling due to metric noise.
2026-03-09 03:05 UTC - Traffic stabilized after manual intervention: increased minReplicas to 2 for the pool and temporarily disabled KEDA scaler. Customer-facing errors dropped to baseline.
2026-03-10 10:00 UTC - Incident debrief; assigned investigation to infra and runtime teams.
2026-03-12 15:30 UTC - Reproduction test: synthetic probe bursts simulated; confirmed readiness probe timeouts create short-lived metric spikes that KEDA treats as sustained load.
2026-03-13 11:00 UTC - Proposed mitigations reviewed in triage and selected a phased rollout plan.
2026-03-13 16:00 UTC - Drafted PRs for metric smoothing and KEDA scaler cooldown configuration (links in comments).
root_cause: Interaction between noisy readiness probe behavior and KEDA custom-metric scaler. The model-server process performs heavyweight JIT and model warmup during container start leading to probe timeouts; readiness probe failures cause temporary metric reporting gaps and synthetic queue spikes (queue_depth metric source aggregated per-pod). KEDA's scaler configuration used a short evaluation window and no smoothing, causing it to interpret transient probe-induced spikes as real load. HPA was configured to scale on CPU but CPU didn't rise immediately because the heavy work occurs in init paths and I/O, so the two autoscalers were out of sync.
impact_summary: Customers experienced elevated error rates (429s) and increased p95 latency for ~45 minutes. The realtime-inference pool had flapping replicas which increased cold-start overhead and temporarily reduced effective capacity. Internal incident page and support tickets logged multiple customer reports; no data loss or security impact.
action_items: Add 30s readiness probe jitter + exponential backoff to model-server probe (owner: Riley Chen, due: 2026-03-18)
Implement metric smoothing / sliding window averaging for 'queue_depth' KEDA scaler (owner: Miguel Santos, due: 2026-03-20)
Increase KEDA stabilization window to 60s and add cooldown period of 120s to avoid reacting to sub-minute spikes (owner: Miguel Santos, due: 2026-03-18)
Introduce an init-warmup sidecar that preloads model artifacts and primes caches to reduce init latency (owner: Priya Nair, due: 2026-04-01)
Add a synthetic canary that exercises readiness probes and exposes probe-failure alerts (owner: Jules Park, due: 2026-03-22)
Update autoscaling runbook: recommended combination of HPA+KEDA settings for realtime-inference (owner: Aisha Patel, due: 2026-03-19)
Run chaos tests that inject short readiness probe failures as part of CI for autoscaler resilience (owner: SRE Team, due: 2026-04-05)
Post-incident customer note and support follow-up summarizing mitigation and timeline (owner: Samir Rao, due: 2026-03-16)
Align metric taxonomy: move queue_depth to per-node aggregated metric and add a pod-level smoothing exporter (owner: Miguel Santos + Observability, due: 2026-03-28)
